title: Forgive and have mercy
hookLine: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful (23:118)

lines: SEND ME BACK, I'LL DO RIGHT.
cards: Some books save the best line for the last page. Al-Mu'minun does something like that. It opened, two days ago, with a bright promise: successful are the believers.
Near its end, it goes somewhere dark. People who have died call out, my Lord, send me back, so that I might do right in what I left behind. And they're told it's only a word they're saying.
Then the surah gathers itself, and its very last verse is a short prayer, handed to the Prophet ﷺ to say.

teach.b: Verse one hundred eighteen. Pickthall: "And (O Muhammad) say: My Lord! Forgive and have mercy, for Thou art Best of all who show mercy." In Arabic: rabbi ghfir warham, wa anta khayru r-rahimin.
Two verbs, ighfir and irham, and they aren't the same request. Ghafara has a sense of covering, of putting something over a fault so it no longer stands exposed. Rahma, mercy, is wider.

It's the root of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim in the bismillah, and many scholars connect it to rahim, the womb: care that surrounds you before you've done anything to earn it. So the prayer asks two things.

teach.h: COVER IT, AND HOLD ME ANYWAY.
teach.b: And hold me anyway. Then it gives the reason: You are the best of those who show mercy. Remember Ayyub, nine days ago, calling God the most merciful of the merciful.
Different surah, close to the same title. And look where the line sits: right after the people who begged to be sent back. They asked for a second chance after it was too late.
This verse is the version you say while there's still time. The surah's bookends are worth noticing too. It begins, qad aflaha l-mu'minun, successful are the believers.
Just before this prayer, it says the deniers will not be successful, la yuflihu.

teach.h: SUCCESS AT BOTH ENDS OF THE SURAH.
teach.b: Success at the start, its lack near the end, and between them, one short sentence anyone can carry.

how: Many Muslims memorize 23:118 and repeat it as a short supplication, often counting it on their fingers or prayer beads after the daily prayers.

o: a reward paid out for good deeds already done
mercy: care that holds you before you've earned it
forgiveness for one sin, asked for by name

games.q: inside the last line — tap the pairs.

s: ighfir and irham mean exactly the same thing
forgiveness covers a fault; mercy is wider care, from the root of ar-Rahman.
23:118 is the last verse of Surah Al-Mu'minun
the surah closes with this short prayer.
in the surah, the people who ask to be sent back are given a second life
they're told it's only a word they're saying. the prayer is for while there's still time.

games.q: the surah opened with 'successful are the believers', then went through a dark scene of people begging to be sent back. how does it end?
o: with a short prayer: forgive and have mercy.
games.why: a short prayer the Prophet is told to say: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful.

practice: If you pray, say the line slowly ten times, in Arabic or English: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, You are the best of the merciful; count on your fingers if that helps.
If you don't pray, let ten breaths go by, and on each one think of something you'd like covered, and someone you'd like to be held.

wordCard.voice: Rahma. Mercy, wider than forgiveness: the last verse of Al-Mu'minun asks God to cover what's wrong and hold us anyway. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: my Lord, forgive and have mercy, from 23:118.

carryVoice: Your line: best of the merciful. Cover what's wrong, and hold me anyway. Day four hundred ninety-one.
